title: First Time With Drops

patient.name: Mr Yeo Chin Huat
patient.presenting_complaint: Newly prescribed eye drops, has never used eye drops before

history.hpc: Mr Yeo says 'Doctor give me eye drop, but I never use before, dunno how.' He needs his charted drop instilled and to be taught the technique so he can do it himself at home.
history.pmhx: No previous eye drop use. No drug allergies (confirm).

va.right: Not the focus of this station
va.left: Not the focus of this station

examination_findings.anterior_segment: No active infection that would change technique

investigations.task: Instil the charted drop and teach a first-time user the correct, safe technique for home
investigations.key_points: Confirm identity, correct eye, drop name/strength and allergy; demonstrate head-back, lower-lid-pocket, one drop, no-touch; have the patient try; teach gentle closure and not to touch the tip

diagnosis: The charted drop is instilled and a first-time user is taught the correct technique: confirming identity, correct eye, the drop and allergy; demonstrating the head-back, lower-fornix, no-touch method; and checking the patient can do it himself. This is a procedural/teaching station.

immediate: Confirm identity, the correct eye and the charted drop and strength
Check for drug/eye-drop allergy before instilling
Perform hand hygiene and explain the steps simply
Demonstrate: tilt head back, pull the lower lid to form a pocket, instil one drop without touching the eye or tip
Have the patient try once with guidance
Teach gentle closure / light pressure near the nose afterwards
Document the drop, eye, time and allergy check
follow_up: Confirm the home schedule and that he can manage alone
Advise reporting stinging, allergy or worsening symptoms
patient_education: Teach the head-back, lower-pocket, one-drop technique in simple language
Stress not touching the bottle tip to the eye or fingers
Reassure that one drop is enough and to keep a routine

key_points: Confirms identity, correct eye and the charted drop
Establishes that the patient is a first-time user
Explains the steps in simple language
Performs hand hygiene and demonstrates the technique
Instils one drop into the lower fornix with a no-touch method
Has the patient try with guidance
Recognises this as a safe-instillation and teaching task
Knows allergy checking is essential before instilling
Understands why a no-touch technique matters
Documents drop, eye, time and allergy check
Confirms the home schedule and self-management
Teaches tip hygiene and one-drop dosing
